name: Heart Women & Girls
mission: We work to promote sexual health, uproot gendered violence, and advance reproductive justice — by establishing choice and access for the most impacted Muslims.
theoryOfChange: HEART Women & Girls has developed a "three-pronged framework" that addresses sexual violence at three levels: individual (Respond with RAHMA), communal (Fulfill your AMANAH), and institutional (Lead with ADALAH). This framework is used to respond to and prevent sexual violence in Muslim communities, exploring barriers and opportunities using a public health framework. This approach is detailed in a document titled "RESPONDING WITH RAHMA:", which outlines how their interventions are expected to lead to change.

strengths_deep_dive: HEART demonstrates strong educational outreach and direct financial support channels for its target community. Through strategic public collaborations, the charity reaches <cite id="5">10,000 incoming students annually at the University of Michigan</cite> with sexual health literacy programming. Professional development efforts have trained <cite id="5">750 service providers and leaders</cite> on gender-based violence and reproductive justice. Beyond direct training, the group operates dedicated financial assistance programs <cite id="5">redistributing $350,000 via mutual aid funds</cite> including <cite id="6">$50,000 directed specifically to survivors of violence</cite> for emergency services.
rich_narrative.summary: Founded in 2010, HEART Women & Girls provides sexual health education, advocacy, research, and training for Muslim communities in the United States <cite id="8">over 15 years of operations</cite>. The organization addresses gender-based violence and reproductive justice through community-focused health literacy programs <cite id="5">and specialized leader training</cite>. In FY2024, the organization reported <cite id="3">$2,016,799 in total revenue</cite> to support its core mission and operations. HEART maintains direct support channels for survivors of violence <cite id="5">through dedicated mutual aid funds</cite>. The group distributes direct financial assistance to survivors <cite id="6">allocating $50,000 for critical survivor services</cite> as part of a larger <cite id="5">$350,000 mutual aid distribution</cite>. Additionally, the organization reaches educational communities through institutional partnerships <cite id="5">engaging 10,000 incoming students annually at the University of Michigan</cite>. Financial filings from FY2024 indicate a <cite id="1">program expense ratio of 74.8%</cite>, meeting the standard sector benchmark for program spending. Fundraising operations remain cost-effective <cite id="1">requiring $0.11 per $1 raised</cite>. HEART holds substantial financial safety margins <cite id="1">maintaining 25.6 months of working capital in reserve</cite>.
